```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, dpi = 150
)

# Set the PROJ path on RCC if needed
proj_data <- file.path(dirname(dirname(R.home())), "share", "proj")
if (dir.exists(proj_data)) {
  Sys.setenv(PROJ_DATA = proj_data)
  Sys.setenv(PROJ_LIB = proj_data)
}

# Packages
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(kableExtra)
library(leaflet)
library(plotly)
library(scales)
library(sf)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)

sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# Plot theme used throughout the descriptive output
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
    )
)

# Project paths
user_name <- Sys.getenv("USER", unset = Sys.info()[["user"]])
repo_dir <- Sys.getenv("RAINFALL_MORTALITY_REPO")
if (repo_dir == "") repo_dir <- file.path("/project/cil/home_dirs", user_name, "repos/rainfall-mortality-2026")

source(file.path(repo_dir, "1_data/mortality_data/1_cleaning/Death_Rates/PHL/paths.R"))

shape_dir <- file.path(post2023_shapefiles_dir, "PH_Adm3_MuniCities.shp")

# Mortality-rate files used below
rate_files <- c(
  adm3_total = file.path(death_rates_dir, "adm3_year_total.csv"),
  adm3_age_broad = file.path(death_rates_dir, "adm3_year_age_broad.csv"),
  national_total = file.path(death_rates_dir, "national_year_total.csv"),
  national_sex = file.path(death_rates_dir, "national_year_sex.csv"),
  national_age_broad = file.path(death_rates_dir, "national_year_age_broad.csv"),
  national_age_broad_sex = file.path(death_rates_dir, "national_year_age_broad_sex.csv"),
  national_age_standard = file.path(death_rates_dir, "national_year_age_standard.csv"),
  national_month_age_broad = file.path(death_rates_dir, "national_month_age_broad.csv")
)

cause_summary_file <- file.path(descriptive_tables_dir, "phl_cause_summary.csv")

# Population files used for the interpolation checks
population_files <- c(
  annual = file.path(population_interpolated_dir, "PHL_population_annual_adm3.csv"),
  census = file.path(population_clean_dir, "census_pop_final.csv"),
  psgc = file.path(admin_geocodes_clean_dir, "psgc_adm_codes.csv")
)

# Keep geography codes as strings so leading zeros are preserved
id_classes <- c(
  shp_adm1_code = "character", shp_adm2_code = "character",
  shp_adm3_code = "character", psgc_adm3_code = "character"
)

# ADM3 mortality-rate files
adm3_total <- fread(rate_files["adm3_total"], colClasses = id_classes) %>%
  as_tibble()

adm3_age_broad <- fread(rate_files["adm3_age_broad"], colClasses = id_classes) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(age_group_broad = factor(age_group_broad, levels = c("0-4", "5-64", "65+")))

# National mortality-rate files
national_sex <- fread(rate_files["national_sex"], showProgress = FALSE) %>% as_tibble()
national_age_broad <- fread(rate_files["national_age_broad"], showProgress = FALSE) %>% as_tibble()
national_age_broad_sex <- fread(rate_files["national_age_broad_sex"], showProgress = FALSE) %>% as_tibble()
national_age_standard <- fread(rate_files["national_age_standard"], showProgress = FALSE) %>% as_tibble()
national_month_age_broad <- fread(rate_files["national_month_age_broad"], showProgress = FALSE) %>% as_tibble()
national_total <- fread(rate_files["national_total"], showProgress = FALSE) %>% as_tibble()

# Cause-of-death summary
cause_summary <- fread(cause_summary_file) %>% as_tibble()

# Population files
annual_pop <- fread(
  population_files["annual"], colClasses = id_classes,
  showProgress = FALSE
) %>% as_tibble()

census_pop <- fread(
  population_files["census"], colClasses = id_classes,
  showProgress = FALSE
) %>% as_tibble()

psgc_pop_controls <- fread(
  population_files["psgc"], colClasses = "character",
  showProgress = FALSE
) %>% as_tibble()
```

# Overview

All rates use place of residence and resident population. Rates are deaths per 100,000 unless stated otherwise.

```{r overview-table}
# Put the main annual mortality measures in one table
year_summary <- national_total %>%
  select(year, deaths, population, crude_rate = death_rate_per_100000) %>%
  left_join(
    national_sex %>%
      select(year, sex, death_rate_per_100000) %>%
      mutate(sex = paste0(sex, "_rate")) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = death_rate_per_100000),
    by = "year"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    national_age_broad %>%
      select(year, age_group_broad, death_rate_per_100000) %>%
      mutate(
        age_group_broad = recode(
          age_group_broad,
          "0-4" = "age_0_4_rate",
          "5-64" = "age_5_64_rate",
          "65+" = "age_65_plus_rate"
        )
      ) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = age_group_broad, values_from = death_rate_per_100000),
    by = "year"
  ) %>%
  arrange(year)

# Format counts and rates for the HTML table
year_summary %>%
  mutate(
    deaths = comma(deaths),
    population = comma(round(population)),
    across(ends_with("_rate"), ~ number(.x, accuracy = 0.1))
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Year", "Deaths", "Population", "Crude rate", "Female rate",
      "Male rate", "0–4 rate", "5–64 rate", "65+ rate"
    ),
    align = "rrrrrrrrr"
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE
  ) %>%
  scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "420px")
```


# National trends

```{r national-rate}
# National crude mortality rate over time
national_rate_plot <- ggplot(national_total, aes(year, death_rate_per_100000)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, color = "#2f5d62") +
  geom_point(size = 1.8, color = "#2f5d62") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2006, 2024, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "National death rate", x = NULL, y = "Deaths per 100,000")

ggplotly(national_rate_plot)
```

```{r national-deaths-population}
# Plot deaths and population separately because they are on very different scales
national_long <- national_total %>%
  select(year, deaths, population) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(deaths, population), names_to = "series", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(series = recode(series, deaths = "Deaths", population = "Population"))

national_deaths_population_plot <- ggplot(national_long, aes(year, value, color = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~series, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2006, 2024, by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  labs(title = "Deaths and population", x = NULL, y = NULL)

ggplotly(national_deaths_population_plot)
```

```{r standard-age-heatmap}
# Order the more detailed age groups from youngest to oldest
standard_age_levels <- c(
  "0", "1-4", "5-14", "15-24", "25-34", "35-44",
  "45-54", "55-64", "65-74", "75-79", "80+"
)

standard_age_rates <- national_age_standard %>%
  mutate(age_group_standard = factor(age_group_standard, levels = standard_age_levels))

# Heatmap makes it easier to see age-specific changes across years
standard_age_heatmap <- ggplot(
  standard_age_rates,
  aes(year, age_group_standard, fill = death_rate_per_100000)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2006, 2024, by = 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma", direction = -1, labels = comma,
    name = "Deaths per 100,000"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Death rate by age group", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

ggplotly(standard_age_heatmap)
```


# Monthly rates

The monthly rate is annualized using the number of days in each month and year.

```{r monthly-rate-heatmap}
# Put broad age groups in the usual order and create a monthly date
monthly_rates <- national_month_age_broad %>%
  mutate(
    age_group_broad = factor(age_group_broad, levels = c("0-4", "5-64", "65+")),
    month_date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", year, month))
  )

# Show monthly variation across age groups and years
monthly_rate_heatmap <- ggplot(
  monthly_rates,
  aes(month_date, age_group_broad, fill = annualized_rate_per_100000_person_years)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.12) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma", direction = -1, labels = comma,
    name = "Annualized rate"
  ) +
  labs(title = "Monthly death rate by broad age group", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

ggplotly(monthly_rate_heatmap)
```


# ADM3 rate distributions

Raw and winsorized views. Winsorization is only for display.

```{r adm3-total-rate-distribution}
# Keep ADM3-years with a valid rate and positive population
adm3_total_dist <- adm3_total %>%
  filter(!is.na(death_rate_per_100000), population > 0)

# Cap plotted values at the 99.9th percentile so a few extreme rates do not
# determine the scale of every figure
adm3_rate_cutoff <- quantile(
  adm3_total_dist$death_rate_per_100000,
  probs = 0.999, na.rm = TRUE
)

adm3_total_dist <- adm3_total_dist %>%
  mutate(
    death_rate_display_per_100000 = if_else(
      death_rate_per_100000 > adm3_rate_cutoff,
      as.numeric(adm3_rate_cutoff), death_rate_per_100000
    ),
    rate_winsorized = death_rate_per_100000 > adm3_rate_cutoff,

    # Keep the original rate in the tooltip even when the plotted value is capped
    tooltip = paste0(
      "ADM3: ", shp_adm3_name, " (", shp_adm3_code, ")",
      "<br>Year: ", year,
      "<br>Deaths: ", comma(round(deaths)),
      "<br>Population: ", comma(round(population)),
      "<br>Rate: ", number(death_rate_per_100000, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000",
      "<br>Winsorized: ", if_else(rate_winsorized, "yes", "no"),
      "<br>Winsorized value: ",
      number(death_rate_display_per_100000, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000"
    )
  )

# Report how much of the distribution is affected by the display cutoff
adm3_total_dist %>%
  summarise(
    `Cutoff percentile` = "99.9%",
    `Cutoff rate` = adm3_rate_cutoff,
    `ADM3-years winsorized` = sum(rate_winsorized),
    `Percent winsorized` = mean(rate_winsorized),
    `Maximum rate` = max(death_rate_per_100000)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Cutoff rate` = number(`Cutoff rate`, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Percent winsorized` = percent(`Percent winsorized`, accuracy = 0.001),
    `Maximum rate` = number(`Maximum rate`, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "html", align = "lrrrr") %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )
```

```{r adm3-total-rate-histogram}
# Compare the raw distribution with the display-winsorized version
adm3_hist_data <- bind_rows(
  adm3_total_dist %>%
    transmute(series = "Raw rates", rate = death_rate_per_100000),
  adm3_total_dist %>%
    transmute(series = "Winsorized rates", rate = death_rate_display_per_100000)
)

p <- adm3_hist_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(rate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 70, fill = "#2f5d62", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~series, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1500)) +
  labs(title = "Rate distribution", x = "Deaths per 100,000", y = "ADM3-years")

ggplotly(p)
```

```{r adm3-total-rate-boxplot}
# Build raw and winsorized versions of the same ADM3-year observations
adm3_box_data <- bind_rows(
  adm3_total_dist %>%
    transmute(
      year, shp_adm3_name, shp_adm3_code, deaths, population,
      rate_winsorized, death_rate_display_per_100000,
      series = "Raw rates", rate = death_rate_per_100000
    ),
  adm3_total_dist %>%
    transmute(
      year, shp_adm3_name, shp_adm3_code, deaths, population,
      rate_winsorized, death_rate_display_per_100000,
      series = "Winsorized rates", rate = death_rate_display_per_100000
    )
) %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year)) %>%

  # Identify observations outside the usual 1.5-IQR whiskers within each year
  group_by(series, year) %>%
  mutate(
    q1 = quantile(rate, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(rate, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr = q3 - q1,
    lower_whisker = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
    upper_whisker = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
    outside_whisker = rate < lower_whisker | rate > upper_whisker
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  # Add details for the interactive outlier points
  mutate(
    tooltip_plot = paste0(
      "ADM3: ", shp_adm3_name, " (", shp_adm3_code, ")",
      "<br>Year: ", year,
      "<br>Deaths: ", comma(round(deaths)),
      "<br>Population: ", comma(round(population)),
      "<br>Rate: ", number(rate, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000",
      "<br>Winsorized: ", if_else(rate_winsorized, "yes", "no"),
      "<br>Winsorized value: ",
      number(death_rate_display_per_100000, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000"
    )
  )

# Plot boxplots without the default outlier points, then add interactive ones
p <- ggplot(adm3_box_data, aes(year, rate)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "#b9d8d8", color = "#244b4f") +
  geom_point(
    data = adm3_box_data %>% filter(outside_whisker),
    aes(text = tooltip_plot),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0),
    alpha = 0.35, size = 0.7, color = "#244b4f"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~series, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Rates by year", x = NULL, y = "Deaths per 100,000")

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r adm3-broad-age-rate-distribution, fig.width=14, fig.height=4.5}
    )
  )

# Raw and winsorized versions for each age group
adm3_age_box_data <- bind_rows(
  adm3_age_dist %>%
    transmute(
      year, age_group_broad, shp_adm3_name, shp_adm3_code,

    ),
  adm3_age_dist %>%
    transmute(
      year, age_group_broad, shp_adm3_name, shp_adm3_code,
      deaths, population, rate_winsorized, death_rate_display_per_100000,
      series = "Winsorized rates", rate = death_rate_display_per_100000
    )
) %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year)) %>%

  # Identify boxplot outliers separately by age group and year
  group_by(series, age_group_broad, year) %>%
  mutate(
    q1 = quantile(rate, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(rate, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr = q3 - q1,
    lower_whisker = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
    upper_whisker = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
    outside_whisker = rate < lower_whisker | rate > upper_whisker
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  # Details shown when hovering over the outlier points
  mutate(
    tooltip = paste0(
      "ADM3: ", shp_adm3_name, " (", shp_adm3_code, ")",
      "<br>Year: ", year,
      "<br>Age group: ", age_group_broad,
      "<br>Deaths: ", comma(round(deaths)),
      "<br>Population: ", comma(round(population)),
      "<br>Rate: ", number(rate, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000",
      "<br>Winsorized: ", if_else(rate_winsorized, "yes", "no"),
      "<br>Winsorized value: ",
      number(death_rate_display_per_100000, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000"
    )
  )

# Compare the age-specific distributions over time
p <- ggplot(adm3_age_box_data, aes(year, rate)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "#decbe4", color = "#4d3b5c") +
  geom_point(

    aes(text = tooltip),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0),

  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
```

# ADM3 maps

```{r read-adm3-shape, include=FALSE}
# Read the current ADM3 boundaries
adm3_shape <- st_read(
  shape_dir, layer = "PH_Adm3_MuniCities.shp", quiet = TRUE
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Format the shapefile PSGC values to match the mortality-rate codes
    shp_adm3_code = str_pad(
      str_replace_all(as.character(adm3_psgc), "[^0-9]", ""),
      width = 10, side = "left", pad = "0"
    ),

    # Fix the two city codes that do not match after the generic padding step
    shp_adm3_code = case_when(
      shp_adm3_code == "0000063108" ~ "0631000000",
      shp_adm3_code == "0000138109" ~ "1381000000",
      adm3_en == "City of Iloilo" ~ "0631000000",
      adm3_en == "City of Parañaque" ~ "1381000000",
      TRUE ~ shp_adm3_code
    )
  ) %>%
  select(shp_adm3_code, geometry)

# Simplify a copy of the boundaries for the interactive maps
adm3_leaflet_shape <- adm3_shape %>%
  st_transform(4326) %>%
  st_simplify(dTolerance = 0.05, preserveTopology = TRUE)

# Check that mortality and shapefile ADM3 codes match before mapping
shape_codes <- sort(unique(adm3_shape$shp_adm3_code))
rate_codes <- sort(unique(adm3_total$shp_adm3_code))

shape_not_rates <- setdiff(shape_codes, rate_codes)
rates_not_shape <- setdiff(rate_codes, shape_codes)

if (length(shape_not_rates) > 0 || length(rates_not_shape) > 0) {
  stop(
    "ADM3 shapefile/rate code mismatch.\n",
    "Shape not rates: ", paste(shape_not_rates, collapse = ", "), "\n",
    "Rates not shape: ", paste(rates_not_shape, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
```


# Interpolated population checks

These checks are for the annual population denominator created by `02_Population/03_interpolate_population.R`.

The main things to check are:

- the annual file exactly reproduces the census years and the 2024 ADM3 total controls
- the national series does not have an obvious artificial kink
- individual ADM3 units with large changes look explainable rather than mechanical errors
- population and growth outliers are not concentrated in a suspicious geography

```{r population-interpolation-build-checks}
# Collapse the annual age-sex file to ADM3 totals
annual_pop_totals <- annual_pop %>%
  group_by(
    year, shp_adm1_code, shp_adm1_name, shp_adm2_code, shp_adm2_name,
    shp_adm3_code, shp_adm3_name, psgc_adm3_code, psgc_adm3_name
  ) %>%
  summarise(population = sum(population, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Build matching ADM3 totals for the census anchor years
census_pop_totals <- census_pop %>%
  group_by(census_year, shp_adm3_code) %>%
  summarise(census_population = sum(population, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Read the 2024 PSGC ADM3 population controls
controls_2024 <- psgc_pop_controls %>%
  transmute(
    psgc_adm3_code = municipalicity_code,
    control_population = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", municipalicity_2024_pop))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(psgc_adm3_code))

# Check that interpolation reproduces the observed census years
census_anchor_check <- annual_pop_totals %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2007, 2010, 2015, 2020)) %>%
  select(year, shp_adm3_code, shp_adm3_name, annual_population = population) %>%
  left_join(
    census_pop_totals,
    by = c("year" = "census_year", "shp_adm3_code")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    anchor_type = "Census",
    anchor_population = census_population,
    difference = annual_population - anchor_population,
    abs_difference = abs(difference)
  ) %>%
  select(
    anchor_type, year, shp_adm3_code, shp_adm3_name,
    annual_population, anchor_population, difference, abs_difference
  )

# Check the final 2024 values against the PSGC controls
control_2024_check <- annual_pop_totals %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  select(
    year, shp_adm3_code, shp_adm3_name, psgc_adm3_code,
    annual_population = population
  ) %>%
  left_join(controls_2024, by = "psgc_adm3_code") %>%
  mutate(
    anchor_type = "2024 PSGC control",
    anchor_population = control_population,
    difference = annual_population - anchor_population,
    abs_difference = abs(difference)
  ) %>%
  select(
    anchor_type, year, shp_adm3_code, shp_adm3_name,
    annual_population, anchor_population, difference, abs_difference
  )

# Combine the census and 2024 checks
population_anchor_check <- bind_rows(census_anchor_check, control_2024_check)

# Summarize whether any anchor observations differ from the annual file
population_anchor_summary <- population_anchor_check %>%
  group_by(anchor_type, year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_adm3 = n(),
    max_abs_difference = max(abs_difference, na.rm = TRUE),
    rows_over_tolerance = sum(abs_difference > 1e-6, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate annual ADM3 changes to identify unusual population series
adm3_population_growth <- annual_pop_totals %>%
  arrange(shp_adm3_code, year) %>%
  group_by(shp_adm3_code) %>%
  mutate(
    lag_population = lag(population),
    annual_change = population - lag_population,
    annual_pct_change = if_else(
      lag_population > 0, annual_change / lag_population, NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r population-anchor-table}
population_anchor_summary %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html", digits = 8,
    col.names = c(
      "Anchor type", "Year", "ADM3 rows",
      "Max absolute difference", "Rows over tolerance"
    )
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )
```

```{r interpolated-adm3-population-sample}
# Pick large, small, and fast-changing ADM3s for closer inspection
sample_large <- annual_pop_totals %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  slice_max(population, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(shp_adm3_code, group = "Largest 2024 population")

sample_small <- annual_pop_totals %>%
  filter(year == 2024, population > 0) %>%
  slice_min(population, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(shp_adm3_code, group = "Smallest 2024 population")

sample_jump <- adm3_population_growth %>%
  filter(!is.na(annual_pct_change)) %>%
  group_by(shp_adm3_code) %>%
  summarise(max_abs_pct_change = max(abs(annual_pct_change)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(max_abs_pct_change, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(shp_adm3_code, group = "Largest annual percent change")

# Keep each selected ADM3/group combination once
sample_adm3 <- bind_rows(sample_large, sample_small, sample_jump) %>%
  distinct(shp_adm3_code, group)

sample_population_plot_data <- annual_pop_totals %>%
  inner_join(sample_adm3, by = "shp_adm3_code")

# Plot the selected population series over the full period
sample_population_plot <- ggplot(
  sample_population_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = year, y = population,
    color = shp_adm3_name, group = shp_adm3_code,
    text = paste0(
      shp_adm3_name,
      "<br>Year: ", year,
      "<br>Population: ", comma(round(population))
    )
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~group, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Population", color = "ADM3",
    title = "Selected ADM3 population time series"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggplotly(sample_population_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r leaflet-map}
# Add popup text to the same mortality-map data
map_data_leaflet <- map_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  left_join(adm3_leaflet_shape, by = "shp_adm3_code") %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  mutate(
    popup_text = paste0(
      "<b>ADM3 code:</b> ", shp_adm3_code,
      "<br><b>Year:</b> ", year,
      "<br><b>Deaths:</b> ", comma(round(deaths)),
      "<br><b>Population:</b> ", comma(round(population)),
      "<br><b>Rate:</b> ",
      number(death_rate_per_100000, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000"
    )
  )

# Common color scale across map years
pal <- colorNumeric(
  palette = "magma",
  domain = map_data_leaflet$death_rate_per_100000,
  reverse = TRUE,
  na.color = "#eeeeee"
)

leaflet_map <- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron)

# Add one switchable layer for each selected year
for (map_year in map_years) {
  layer_data <- map_data_leaflet %>%
    filter(year == map_year)

  leaflet_map <- leaflet_map %>%
    addPolygons(
      data = layer_data,
      group = as.character(map_year),
      fillColor = ~pal(death_rate_per_100000),
      fillOpacity = 0.75,
      color = "#444444",
      weight = 0.2,
      opacity = 0.6,
      popup = ~popup_text,
      highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
        weight = 1.2, color = "#111111", bringToFront = TRUE
      )
    )
}

# Show the most recent year by default
leaflet_map %>%
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = pal,
    values = map_data_leaflet$death_rate_per_100000,
    title = "Deaths per 100,000",
    labFormat = labelFormat(transform = function(x) round(x, 0))
  ) %>%
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = as.character(map_years),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  hideGroup(as.character(map_years[-length(map_years)]))
```

```{r sparse-flags-leaflet-map}
# Summarize zero rates, extreme rates, and small populations for each ADM3
sparse_flags <- adm3_total %>%
  filter(!is.na(death_rate_per_100000), population > 0) %>%
  group_by(shp_adm3_code) %>%
  summarise(
    shp_adm3_name = first(shp_adm3_name),
    max_rate = max(death_rate_per_100000, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate = min(death_rate_per_100000, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_population = min(population, na.rm = TRUE),
    zero_rate_years = sum(death_rate_per_100000 == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    extreme_100k_years = sum(death_rate_per_100000 >= 100000, na.rm = TRUE),
    extreme_10k_years = sum(death_rate_per_100000 >= 10000, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  # Combine the sparse/extreme indicators used for the map
  mutate(
    flag_count =
      as.integer(max_rate >= 100000) +
      as.integer(max_rate >= 10000) +
      as.integer(min_rate == 0) +
      as.integer(min_population < 100) +
      as.integer(min_population < 500),
    flag_group = case_when(
      max_rate >= 100000 ~ "Rate >= 100,000",
      max_rate >= 10000 ~ "Rate >= 10,000",
      min_rate == 0 & min_population < 500 ~ "Zero rate and small population",
      min_rate == 0 ~ "Zero rate",
      min_population < 500 ~ "Small population",
      TRUE ~ "No sparse flag"
    )
  )

# Add the flags and summary statistics to the boundaries
sparse_map <- adm3_leaflet_shape %>%
  left_join(sparse_flags, by = "shp_adm3_code") %>%
  mutate(
    popup_text = paste0(
      "<b>ADM3:</b> ", shp_adm3_name, " (", shp_adm3_code, ")",
      "<br><b>Flag group:</b> ", flag_group,
      "<br><b>Flag count:</b> ", flag_count,
      "<br><b>Max rate:</b> ", number(max_rate, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000",
      "<br><b>Min rate:</b> ", number(min_rate, accuracy = 0.1), " per 100,000",
      "<br><b>Min population:</b> ", comma(round(min_population)),
      "<br><b>Zero-rate years:</b> ", zero_rate_years,
      "<br><b>Years rate >= 10,000:</b> ", extreme_10k_years,
      "<br><b>Years rate >= 100,000:</b> ", extreme_100k_years
    )
  )

# Fixed colors for the sparse/extreme categories
sparse_pal <- colorFactor(
  palette = c("#4d4d4d", "#d73027", "#fc8d59", "#91bfdb", "#4575b4", "#fdae61"),
  domain = c(
    "No sparse flag", "Rate >= 100,000", "Rate >= 10,000",
    "Zero rate and small population", "Zero rate", "Small population"
  ),
  na.color = "#eeeeee"
)

# Map where zero/extreme rates and small populations occur
leaflet(sparse_map, options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) %>%
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~sparse_pal(flag_group),
    fillOpacity = 0.75,
    color = "#444444",
    weight = 0.2,
    opacity = 0.6,
    popup = ~popup_text,
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 1.2, color = "#111111", bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = sparse_pal,
    values = ~flag_group,
    title = "Sparse/extreme flag"
  )
```
